study type: Experimental animal study (cohort), in vitro cell study, and human observational (cross-sectional)
outcome: Cholesterol phenotype of high cardiovascular disease risk
3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (Hmgcr) histone acetylation and expression
HMGCR expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) (human)
cohort: The study included pregnant Wistar rats and their female offspring, bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) hepatoid differentiated cells and HepG2 cell lines, and human female neonates whose mothers received dexamethasone treatment during pregnancy.
finding: Prenatal dexamethasone exposure in rats causes persistent enhancement of hepatic cholesterol synthesis function before and after birth through the GR/miR-133a-3p/Sirt1 pathway, ultimately leading to increased hypercholesterolemia susceptibility in female offspring.
gest_age: Dexamethasone exposure in rats was from gestational day 9 to 20, with fetal collection at gestational day 21.
